headline: WASDE TOMORROW; GRAINS SOFT, CRUDE RUNS
subheadline: Corn and wheat give back ground ahead of Tuesday's report while WTI adds 2.6% on fresh geopolitical freight risk.
lead: The market is doing what it does the day before a WASDE: not much. Corn settled at $4.38, off 3.75 cents. Wheat gave back 6.5 cents to $6.46. The funds aren't adding conviction either direction with tomorrow's numbers still in the envelope. Crude ran to $80.84 on Kazakhstan rerouting headlines and that's the loudest thing that happened today. Wait on grains.
the_takeaway: Hold tight: WASDE tomorrow sets the grain story for the next four weeks.
teaser: WASDE eve, grains drift, crude runs -- here's what to watch Tuesday.

one_number.unit: of China's annual US soybean target already bought
one_number.context: China's purchases since the May summit are roughly a quarter of the $17B annual commitment. That pace, if it holds, outpaces typical seasonal buying and is one reason beans at $11.60 aren't breaking lower ahead of tomorrow's WASDE.

yesterdays_call.summary: Called corn down, toward below $4.45; corn closed today at $4.385, through that level.
yesterdays_call.note: The call played out: WASDE-eve positioning drained conviction from the board and corn drifted to $4.385, through the $4.45 target. Funds sat on their hands and the tape did the work.

sections.title: GRAINS SOFT AHEAD OF WASDE
sections.body:
- Corn Dec '26 settled at **$4.62**, off 3.5 cents, with no fresh fundamental reason to move; the funds are sitting on their hands the day before USDA prints new supply-demand numbers.
- Wheat at $6.46 gave back 6.5 cents; the weather story that briefly lifted it last week hasn't produced new headlines, and without a fresh catalyst the short sellers own the afternoon.
- Soybeans nearby held the best of a bad lot, up 3 cents to $11.60, underpinned by the China-pace story: purchases since the May summit are running roughly 25% toward the annual commitment, which is early-season heat for a demand floor.
sections.catalyst: China soybean purchase pace running ahead of seasonal norms, per Farm Policy News.
sections.bottom_line: WASDE tomorrow at 11 AM CT resets everything; today's drift is the market clearing the decks.
sections.farmer_action: If you have old-crop corn to move, the WASDE is a defined risk event; price ahead of the print or set a target and let the market come to you.

sections.title: CATTLE HOLDS; FEEDERS EASE
sections.body:
- Live cattle firmed a quarter percent to **$232.40**, but the recovery is thin: the Cargill multi-plant lockout, ongoing since May 19, is still removing roughly 6,000 head of daily processing capacity, and that processing constraint, not demand, is what's holding the board.
- Feeders slipped 0.7% to $349.30, continuing to price in the Aug 24 Douglas, AZ phased border reopening for Mexican feeder imports; the screwworm closure has tightened feeder supply all summer and the market is now looking past that scarcity.
sections.catalyst: Aug 24 Mexican border phased reopening and ongoing Cargill lockout both threading into price structure.
sections.bottom_line: Cattle's ceiling is the packer; feeders' floor is the border date.

sections.title: CRUDE RUNS ON FREIGHT RISK
sections.body:
- WTI added 2.6% to **$80.84**, its sharpest single-session gain in several weeks, after Kazakhstan announced it is actively rerouting crude exports away from the Black Sea terminal at Novorossiysk following continued Ukrainian drone pressure on Russian energy infrastructure.
- Money managers actually cut bullish bets on WTI for a second straight week per COT data through Aug 4, so the fund setup coming into today was lean-long; a geopolitical freight headline hits harder into that positioning than it would into a crowded long.
- Natural gas added 2.5% to $2.80, though it sits at just 6% of its 52-week range; the move is real on a percentage basis but the absolute level is still historically soft.
sections.catalyst: Kazakhstan crude rerouting from Black Sea, drone strikes on Tatarstan refinery hub.
sections.bottom_line: Diesel, not crude, is the fall fieldwork input story; crude running does not immediately change harvest-cost math.

sections.title: CROP PROGRESS AT 3 PM CT
sections.body:
- USDA Crop Progress drops at 3:00 PM CT today; corn is in dough-to-dent and soybeans are filling pods, so the ratings print carries real weight: good-to-excellent above last week's reading confirms the 2026 growing season's clean crop story, a step down opens the door for a weather-premium bid ahead of WASDE.
- AGSIST's ratings-based nowcast has corn at **184.1 bu/acre** against USDA trend of 183.0; the crop tour the week of Aug 17 is the next real-world check on those numbers.
- Today's Crop Progress is the last major read before WASDE prints tomorrow; if ratings slip, the Aug 12 report may carry a downward yield adjustment.
sections.catalyst: USDA Crop Progress, 3:00 PM CT Monday (per calendar schedule).
sections.bottom_line: Ratings hold the line, WASDE confirms; ratings slip, WASDE becomes a live event.
sections.farmer_action: Watch the 3 PM CT print: good-to-excellent corn below last week's level adds basis risk ahead of harvest.

outside_the_pit.title: AGP and Port of Grays Harbor Open Major Export Terminal
outside_the_pit.body: Terminal 4 at Grays Harbor went live this week, with the capacity to more than double ag commodity exports through the Pacific Northwest port. More throughput on the West Coast is structural support for basis in corn and beans over the next several years.

outside_the_pit.title: JBS Sells $2.5B Stake in Australian Operations to Indonesia Sovereign Fund
outside_the_pit.body: JBS is bringing Danantara into a joint venture covering Australia, New Zealand, and Southeast Asia with up to $5B in growth capital attached. Global packer consolidation keeps moving; watch how this repositions JBS's US beef priorities into 2027.

weekly_thread.question: Does the WASDE on Tuesday confirm a record or near-record corn yield, and does that break Dec corn below $4.50?
weekly_thread.status_text: Grains are drifting soft into the print; the answer comes Tuesday at 11 AM CT when USDA sets the official yield number against a market sitting at $4.62 Dec.

the_more_you_know.title: WASDE Eve Is Its Own Forecast
the_more_you_know.body: The day before a WASDE, price drift without a news catalyst is actually information. When the funds have conviction ahead of a report, they show up. When they sit, it means the market's probability distribution is wide. A flat-to-soft grain board today says the trade genuinely doesn't know which way tomorrow's yield number lands.

watch_list.desc: USDA Crop Progress: corn good-to-excellent below last week's reading adds weather premium; above it, the bear case holds.
August WASDE: corn yield above 183.5 bu/acre is the line that keeps Dec corn below $4.62; below 182.0 reopens the upside.
Weekly Export Sales: soybean sales under 300K MT say China's purchase pace is slowing; above 500K confirms the demand floor is real.
Pro Farmer Crop Tour begins; their field numbers are the first real-world check on USDA's WASDE yield estimates.

daily_quote.text: Many a mickle makes a muckle.
